verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_filter_blocks_xss: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Docstrings are present and the token-branch comments are numbered ("# 5. Script tag"), but the long quote-check conditions are repeated in several places (val.startswith('"') and val.endswith('"')) or ...). `_filter_html_single_pass` is about 130 lines and hard to follow.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: `_filter_html_single_pass` is a single function of more than 100 lines (cap applies). The quote-stripping block is copy-pasted 3 times (is_dangerous_url, style, srcdoc). The allow/deny lists are inline tuples, not named constants as the conventions ask. ATTR_REGEX is recompiled on every filter_attributes call.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: `except Exception: pass` around the base64 decode in is_dangerous_url (cap: at most accept). Magic tuples of MIME types and schemes are inline. Positives: an explicit encoding with surrogateescape, and argv and file-existence checks.

items.name: Obfuscated vectors neutralised
items.evidence: Uses general rules: case-insensitive on* removal, entity decoding, control-char stripping, a scheme check on every attribute value, and recursive srcdoc filtering. There is no element deny-list for iframe/object/embed/base/math/svg; it relies only on URL checks. The hidden test_filter_blocks_xss failed.

items.name: Minimal edits on dirty documents
items.name_zh: 含恶意内容的文档仅做最小修改
items.evidence: The tokenising approach keeps the original quoting and whitespace. However, it drops any attribute whose value begins with javascript:, including benign ones like title. It also edits comments, and the hidden test_clean_html_unchanged failed, which shows it changes benign markup.
